correctness.rationale: The exact implicit sample equation z+r(1-alpha)f(z)=alpha x is strictly increasing in z for every monotone Lipschitz f; the mesh map is well defined. Subtracting two instances gives m(sigma)=(beta-r(alpha-beta)sigma)/(1+r(1-alpha)sigma), strictly decreasing in secant slope sigma in [0,L]; -1<m(L) iff (1+beta)>rL(2alpha-1-beta). Therefore if d=2alpha-1-beta<=0 any finite gain contracts; otherwise rL<(1+beta)/d is uniform sharp, with f(y)=Ly a boundary counterexample. For tanh at rcrit, every nonzero |F(x)|<|x| and analytic expansion F(x)=-x+c x^3+O(x^5), c=(1+beta)d^3/(3alpha(1-beta)^3), implies asymptotic (2ck)^(-1/2). The odd map has the unique antisymmetric branch because tanh(z)/z decreases from 1 to 0; derivative sech^2 z<tanh(z)/z makes its two-step multiplier <1. Independent SymPy calculation rederived m and c identities exactly. Local, not global, attraction of supercritical branch is proved.
